issues.legal_issue: A fictitious entry in a land record cannot confer statutory occupancy rights merely because a public official made it while performing official duties.
material_facts: The claimed occupancy rights depended on an entry recording the claimant’s predecessor as an occupant in a land record.
The entry was found to be false, made through irregular methods, and contrary to the rules governing preparation and checking of the records.
The official’s entry had been treated as sufficient to confer occupancy rights despite its lack of genuineness.
issues.conclusion: The fictitious entry could not confer occupancy rights. The High Court’s orders were set aside, leaving in place the consolidation authorities’ orders expunging the respondents’ names and recording the appellants’ names.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 20(b)(i) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, the relevant entry must be made in a khasra or khatauni prepared under the applicable law. Sections 28 and 33 of the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901, and the U.P. Land Records Manual’s instructions on investigation, preparation, and checking of entries require a lawful record-making process. A fictitious entry is not genuine and cannot confer adhivasi rights; an entry made through ill-will or irregular methods does not become authentic merely because a Patwari made it in the course of official duties. The Court relied on Sonawati v. Sriram and Ram Das v. Deputy Director of Consolidation.

predicates.claim_for_statutory_occupancy_status_bas: A person claims statutory occupancy status on the basis of a land record.
predicates.record_entry_is_basis_of_claim: The claimed status depends on the relevant entry in that record.
predicates.entry_is_fictitious: The entry is not genuine, including because it was introduced falsely or through irregular methods.

issues.definition: When a claim to statutory occupancy status depends on a land-record entry and that entry is fictitious, the entry does not confer that status.
